ownership_reason:
Only the gold calls the visitor and takes each node's children: hop 1 makes the namespace-aware builder and the new W3C document, hop 2 sets the document URI and creates the W3CBuilder visitor, hop 3 picks the document's root element and hop 4 passes it on. The gold's javadoc promises a depth-first traverse of the root and all of its descendants for a NodeVisitor, whose head and tail are documented as the start tag and the end tag of a node, i.e. a walk in document order; the variant pushes each node's children onto its stack without reversing them, so they come off last-first and W3CBuilder writes every child list in reverse. No one-line change above the gold restores the order: a hop cannot wrap the visitor without a new type, the walk must start at the document's first element (the Document node's tag name '#root' is rejected by createElementNS), and walking the root's children one by one leaves out the root's head.
